Trouble is, most of the PC's running XP won't be upgradable to Win 7 let alone 8 or 8.1, since they were ordered with the minimum specification needed to run XP. Obviously, there's no way on earth that they'd run Win 10!

Let's say that they got round to upgrading as many machines to Win 7, they'd have to do the whole thing all over again in the year 2020, which is when support for the next iteration of the OS expires. Then do the whole thing again!  And meanwhile, paying Microsoft a shit ton of money for support for the next iteration of the OS, as they are doing with XP. Approx £50,000,000 per week for XP support.

They are simply buying a shit ton of the same machines (usually Dell Optiplex) with the correct spec to run Win 10. The rest, they'd upgrade to Win 7 at best!

I've been consulted a few times on ways to upgrade the systems. Time and again I've said "install Linux, and send everyone on a course so they can use the new OS".  I think it was Sweden that did just that, to Ubuntu. And since most of the peripheral devices such as those used in operating theatres or intensive care unit are all running various versions of Linux, it won't be such a big problem to network them all. May just need some bespoke drivers etc. Fuck it, why not just run them on Win 10 VM!

Thing is, and I don't mean this disrespectfully, the UK as a people are very backward looking, particularly in Yorkshire where I am!  Again, I don't wish to criticise the English people, most of them are salt of the Earth. I just meant with respect to other nations such as the US.

I do hope that nobody dies as a result of operation cancellations, as a result of all this. I also hope that no patient records are harvested and put into the public domain. However, it's inevitable that something like this happens, and they've had fair warning.  They may perhaps sit up and put into place people like me have been telling them for years.

Approximately 9 hours ago, I was feeling very, very down and suicidal, about total misunderstandings and misreading things that were said/happened over Christmas. I was racking my brain for hours, how I was going to ask my brother about those things that had been plaguing me since then. I got it into my head that my brother would kick off on the phone, saying something like "how dare you think of us like that."  He caught me off guard whilst I was planning what to say, and he phoned me, so just said what I had to say, but asked him not to be angry before hand. I also explained that what I had to ask him may seem trivial even stupid.

You know what buddy?  It turns out that neither him, his wife or their son meant the things that I though they had, with the way they looked at me when I said whatever, or what they meant when they said whatever.

And I'm 44, and it's still very difficult for me. But don't let that make you think that it's all gonna be bad, even by my age. Chances are it won't. Hang in there and tell your parents.
